safetyBoundary.note: This delta records unsigned QA only; it does not alter the previously submitted application.

findings.summary: Three conditional explanation controls are official textarea elements with maxLength=4000. Empty OTHER and NOT EMPLOYED attempts produced branch-specific server errors; the NOT EMPLOYED filled path advanced.
findings.limits: The output stores no entered text. The OTHER filled transition is not isolated in the raw point-check names.

findings.summary: Family2 spouse date uses separate day/month/year controls. The year-only and full-date paths both reached Work; readback confirmed blank finer parts for the year-only path, but values are excluded from the artifact.
findings.limits: This does not assert date behavior for unrelated fields or all invalid dates.

findings.summary: CEAC rejected duplicate former-spouse identity even when other details differed; a different given name advanced. The count control is text/maxLength=2 and the row explanation is textarea/maxLength=4000.
findings.limits: Only the tested identity combinations are recorded.

findings.summary: All 27 Yes branches exposed individual Explain textareas with maxLength=4000. Empty explanations were rejected; TEST DESCRIPTION filled Parts 1–4 and Next advanced. Part 5 was accepted on Back because the Next-to-Photo control was unavailable in this unsigned QA run. The independent security5 navigation supplement separately records the disabled Next button and successful top PHOTO-link navigation.
findings.limits: Part 5 Next remained disabled in the captured states; final signature/submission remain unknown. The top PHOTO-link navigation is documented only in companionEvidence.security5Navigation. No/hide evidence is not re-created per question in this delta.
findings.companionEvidence: local production React harness: 27/27 yes shows textarea max4000 and no detaches it; console errors 0. This is separate from the CEAC point-check/server-validation evidence.

findings.summary: Specific travel Yes exposed split departure controls and the filled flow advanced to companions.
findings.limits: All date validity permutations remain out of scope.

findings.summary: The CEAC start page exposes the consular-post selector with the observed ucLocation_ddlLocation control and 218 options.
findings.limits: This is a public DOM/control observation; it does not prove every location option or downstream server acceptance path.

fields.positiveEvidence: Other marital status exposed a textarea with tag=textarea and maxLength=4000.
fields.negativeEvidence: The No/hidden side was not isolated in this fresh point-check delta.
fields.validationEvidence: A later empty submission returned a shared-page invalid marital status error; the explanation field was not isolated from the other missing controls.
fields.caveat: DOM shape is direct evidence; standalone requiredness remains unresolved in this delta.

fields.positiveEvidence: Passport type OTHER exposed Explain as a textarea with maxLength=4000.
fields.negativeEvidence: The non-OTHER side was not isolated in this fresh point-check delta.
fields.validationEvidence: No isolated empty/filled submission result is present in this delta.
fields.caveat: DOM shape is direct evidence; standalone requiredness remains unknown here.

fields.positiveEvidence: The same official textarea control is exposed for OTHER and NOT EMPLOYED branches; the control is textarea/maxLength=4000.
fields.negativeEvidence: No branch-specific hidden snapshot is used because CEAC reuses the same control ID.
fields.validationEvidence: OTHER empty Next returned “Specify Other has not been completed.”; NOT EMPLOYED empty Next returned “Explain has not been completed.” and the filled NOT EMPLOYED flow advanced with no error.
fields.caveat: The raw state names do not store applicant text and do not prove the OTHER filled transition; the NOT EMPLOYED required/accepted path is captured.

fields.positiveEvidence: Family2 spouse/partner DOM exposes the shared day control; the current point-checks include the spouse year-only and full-date transitions.
fields.negativeEvidence: No hidden/conditional side was asserted for this date part.
fields.validationEvidence: Year-only spouse date reached Work with blank day/month; a later full day/month/year entry also reached Work. Raw values are intentionally omitted.
fields.caveat: The generic CEAC IDs are scoped by the Family2 page and state; they are not the Personal1 DOB controls.

fields.positiveEvidence: Number of Former Spouses is a text input with maxLength=2.
fields.negativeEvidence: No select options were observed for this control.
fields.validationEvidence: Three populated rows were observed; a duplicate identity submission was rejected by CEAC.
fields.caveat: The DOM maxlength does not establish the complete server numeric range.

fields.positiveEvidence: Former spouse row 0 exposes a textarea with maxLength=4000.
fields.negativeEvidence: No hidden/alternate control was asserted.
fields.validationEvidence: No isolated length or requiredness submission was performed for this textarea in the fresh delta.
fields.caveat: Repeat row 1/2 controls are present in the three-row state; this row is the stable row-0 representative.

fields.positiveEvidence: Rows with a different given name (same surname/DOB) advanced to Work.
fields.negativeEvidence: Same surname/given name/DOB was rejected as “You cannot enter a duplicate Former Spouse”; changing other details alone still rejected.
fields.validationEvidence: The duplicate error appeared in both duplicate test states; the different-given-name state had no errors.
fields.caveat: This is a tested CEAC cross-row rule, not a claim that every possible identity combination was exhausted.

fields.positiveEvidence: Specific-travel YES exposes day/month/year departure controls.
fields.negativeEvidence: Specific-travel NO and its hidden controls were not isolated in this point-check record.
fields.validationEvidence: After the specific travel details were filled, Next advanced to complete_travelcompanions.aspx.
fields.caveat: This proves the observed filled transition; all date validity permutations remain out of scope for this delta.
